strings.sweep.help: Find the fastest clock the card reads correctly at
strings.sweep_fastest: Fastest verified: %.3f MHz at %.1f KiB/s (%.2f MiB/s), %.2fx the reference.
strings.sweep_header: Clock sweep over %s, %u KiB read per step from sector 0.
strings.sweep_high_speed_note: That first failure is the step where the driver begins attempting the high-speed switch, which it only does above %d kHz. The switch runs at the 400 kHz init clock, before the bus is ever set to the requested rate, so this is a protocol threshold rather than a signal limit -- requesting %d kHz fails where %d kHz works. Suspect the card's high-speed handling, not the board.
strings.sweep_host_limited: Limited by the host, not the card: every request above %d kHz produced the same %.3f MHz, so the card was never clocked any faster than that. %s cannot drive it harder on this interface.
strings.sweep_no_failures: No failures up to the %d kHz ceiling that was asked for; raise it to look further.
strings.sweep_overclocked_note: This is %.3f MHz above the card's rated %.3f MHz. Passing one read sweep is not a stability guarantee: overclocking is out of spec, and margin varies with temperature, supply and wiring.
strings.sweep_readonly_note:
Measurement is read-only: nothing is written to the card at a clock
that has not been verified. The results file is written at the end,
at the fastest rate that passed.
strings.sweep_reference:
Reference CRC 0x%08X, stable over two passes. Card is rated for %.3f MHz at default speed;
that rises if it accepts the high-speed switch, which is only attempted above %d kHz.
strings.sweep_reinit_failed: Re-initializing at %d kHz after the sweep: %s
strings.sweep_same_clock: %7d kHz  %7.3f MHz            -   same clock as the previous step, skipped
strings.sweep_within_spec: Within spec: the card is rated for %.3f MHz at this setting, so nothing here was an overclock.

strings.uhs_unsupported: %d kHz selects a UHS-I mode, which %s does not support. Ask for a nearby rate such as %d kHz instead.
